review_output: {"summary":"I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR issues in the supplied code. All three earlier repairs check out: the studio key includes the account ID, connection validation only succeeds if all five stored encrypted credential fields still match what was read, and an unknown accountId returns notFound. The account-specific webhook route re-exports the shared POST handler; whether that handler correctly checks the accountId param is taken from your description of the regression test, since the parent route source wasn't included. Project switching and the delivery worker's claim both use Serializable transactions over the same project and delivery rows, so a switch can't race an in-flight push. The worker also re-checks the selected account after claiming, and the duplicate null-account guard you removed is covered by the active-status check. I'm reporting three low-severity items.","findings":[{"area":"Account lifecycle authority","confidence":0.45,"file":"src/app/actions/line-actions.ts","impact":"If any flow disables an account for safety or compliance, an owner can bring it back into project selection and notification delivery just by re-saving its credentials.","issue":"saveLineOfficialAccountAction sets status to \"active\" on every update, so re-saving a disabled account turns it back on.","required_test":"Disable an existing account, re-save its credentials, and check that the status stays disabled, or that reactivation is explicit and audited.","evidence":"The update data is { ...protectedCredentials, displayName, status: \"active\", ... } and is applied to both create and update with no check of existing.status.","recommended_fix":"Keep existing.status on update and only set status to active on create, unless reactivation is an intended, audited operation.","severity":"MINOR"},{"area":"Connection diagnostic","confidence":0.6,"file":"src/app/actions/line-actions.ts","impact":"A disabled account can be shown as recently validated, which is misleading. The risk is low because the UI disables the button, but a direct action call bypasses that.","issue":"testLineOfficialAccountAction does not check status, so it calls LINE and records lastValidatedAt for non-active accounts.","required_test":"Call the action directly for a non-active account and check that it returns not_configured without updating lastValidatedAt.","evidence":"The select does not include status, and the updateMany where clause has no status: \"active\" condition.","recommended_fix":"Select status and return not_configured when it isn't active, or add status: \"active\" to the CAS where clause.","severity":"NIT"},{"area":"Rich menu draft scoping","confidence":0.5,"file":"src/app/actions/line-rich-menu-actions.ts","impact":"Not exploitable today, because a draft's account ID only changes from null to an ID when the first account is created. But if drafts ever become reassignable, a stale form could edit the wrong account's draft.","issue":"In editDraft, the delete and update writes filter only on vendorId plus id/revision and leave out lineOfficialAccountId, so account binding depends on an earlier read rather than the write itself.","required_test":"Check that a delete or update posted with a mismatched accountId but a valid id/revision changes no rows.","evidence":"deleteMany({ where: { vendorId, ...reference } }) and updateMany({ where: { vendorId, ...reference } }), while the earlier read used lineOfficialAccountId: accountId.","recommended_fix":"Add lineOfficialAccountId: accountId to the deleteMany and updateMany where clauses.","severity":"NIT"}]}
